messages:
DevOps-Bot: PAGER P0 — GPU host instability detected in us-west1 (node gpu-prod-27). Autoscaling and serving metrics triggered alerts. Investigate please: https://incidents.internal/1794506789 :rotating_light:
Ava (oncall): Acked. I'm on it — switching channel to this thread for coordination. Brief summary pls, infra hooks + customer impact?
Eli (SRE): Seeing repeated PCIe AER logs and ECC corrected error counts rising. Node rebooted automatically at 23:12:41 UTC then again at 23:29:05 UTC. Kernel reports: `aer: pci id 10de:1b80 slot 0000:65:00.0: AER: multiple
errors, severity=corrected`
Maya (ML Infra): Which pools/allocations were on that host? Any dedicated customers?
Infra-Observer-Bot: Host: gpu-prod-27 (g5.16xlarge), AZ: us-west1-b, running containerd. Active pods: 18, including 3 Dedicated (customer-dk, customer-xl, customer-ops).
Benji (Support): Heads up — customer-dk reported elevated latencies at 23:09 UTC via support ticket INC-8921. They saw request timeouts and retries.
Ava (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Drain node, 2) Migrate affected pods to warm pool, 3) Temporarily pin dedicated customers to fallback pool. I will start drain now.
Carla (Eng Runtime): +1. Suggest enabling degraded-mode routing for steady-state chat sessions to avoid cold restarts. Also enable prefix cache disable for customers migrating to new node to avoid stale KV hits.
Ava (oncall): Running: `kubectl cordon gpu-prod-27 && kubectl drain gpu-prod-27 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
Eli (SRE): Logs attached below (snip):
```
[23:08:58] nvidia: ECC corrected: 12
[23:09:02] kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error detected
[23:12:41] systemd: Reboot initiated: watchdog triggered
[23:29:05] systemd: Reboot initiated: kernel panic? stack trace dumped
[23:30:10] nvidia: Device recovered
```
Maya (ML Infra): Noted. From scheduler metrics, 7 pods failed to reschedule automatically due to IP exhaustion in that subnet — we had to allocate from burst pool. That increased cold-start tail latencies.
Benji (Support): Customer-dk notice: "we saw 503s for ~3 minutes and SDK retries recovered". Impact window in ticket: 23:08–23:12 UTC. They did not lose data, just elevated latency and a few failed calls.
Ava (oncall): Hypotheses (initial):
- H1: Noisy neighbor on same host causing PCIe AER flood -> ECC counts go up -> driver/kernel panic -> node reboot
- H2: Underlying hardware fault (memory module/GPU ECC) causing spontaneous reboots
- H3: Cloud hypervisor/firmware bug triggered by high PCIe throughput from another tenant
Please add evidence or tests below.
Eli (SRE): Evidence for H1: GPU PCIe bandwidth counters spiked at 23:07:50 (see perf dump). We pulled dmesg from the host — AERs correlate with bandwidth bursts. Also other VMs on the same rack reported elevated NIC errors around same time.
Carla (Eng Runtime): Runtime logs show KV-cache misses spiking just before the error window — could be unrelated but lines up with heavy model loads around 23:06–23:09.
Infra-Observer-Bot: Collected artifacts uploaded to /shared/incidents/1794506789/: dmesg.log, nvml-stats.json, perf-top.csv, kube-events.json, support-ticket-threads.txt
Maya (ML Infra): Quick check: both reroute and dedicated fallback succeeded for customer-xl and customer-ops. Customer-dk was on a dedicated instance with no active failover; we migrated them manually to fallback pool at 23:13 UTC.
Benji (Support): Posting a short customer impact blurb to ops-status: "Partial service disruption for some inference requests in us-west1 between 23:08–23:13 UTC. Automated retries succeeded for most customers; a small number of dedicated instances required manual migration. Engineering investigating root cause." :white_check_mark:
Ava (oncall): Current mitigations completed: node cordoned + drained, pods rescheduled, dedicated customers moved to fallback pools, alert thresholds raised for AER/ECC corrected counts. Rebooted host is quarantined by cloud provider.
Eli (SRE): Next actions for RCA: request cloud support open ticket for hardware trace, request host serial logs, ask provider for migration/vm-activity timeline. I'll also pull nvme SMART and GPU ECC history.
Maya (ML Infra): Can someone grep model-serving logs for 23:05–23:10 to fetch request patterns? I suspect a large batched job hit the host.
Carla (Eng Runtime): I'll search routing logs and fetch per-customer request histogram. ETA 10m.
Ava (oncall): Handing off on-call to Eli in 10 minutes. Eli, you have the pager. I'll update incident channel and my replacement note.
Eli (SRE): I have the pager. Will continue timeline and hypothesis tracking.
Infra-Observer-Bot: Incident state: mitigated -> partial recover. Severity remains P0 until provider confirms hardware health.
Eli (SRE): Timeline (working):
- 23:05:30 UTC — sustained high model token throughput observed on host gpu-prod-27 (runtime spikes)
- 23:07:50 UTC — PCIe bandwidth spike recorded, AER events begin
- 23:08:58 UTC — ECC corrected errors increment
- 23:09:30 UTC — client retries escalate (support ticket entries)
- 23:12:41 UTC — host auto-reboot (watchdog)
- 23:13:00 UTC — manual migration of dedicated customer-dk to fallback pool
- 23:29:05 UTC — second unplanned reboot observed (post-recovery instability)
- 23:35:00 UTC — host quarantined by cloud provider for deeper diagnostics
Maya (ML Infra): For the RCA doc I'll need: nvml-stats.json, perf-top.csv, kube events, model request traces for 23:03–23:15. Infra-Observer-Bot already uploaded some. Please add any customer logs to /shared/incidents/1794506789/others
Benji (Support): I'll draft a customer-facing follow-up for the affected customers summarizing impact and current status. Will coordinate with legal for wording if needed.
Carla (Eng Runtime): Note: runtime will add a guard on batching size per host to avoid saturating PCIe concurrently with other tenants. I'll open an internal RFC for an emergency rate-limiter.
Eli (SRE): Preliminary root-cause direction leans to H1 (noisy neighbor / PCIe saturation) given correlation of bandwidth spikes + AERs + NIC errors in rack. But we need provider logs to rule out firmware/hardware faults.
Ava (oncall): Thanks team — I'll post a short post-incident note once we have provider confirmation. Handing off officially to Eli now. :handshake:
Eli (SRE): Taking over. If anyone finds additional anomalies (storage SMART, BMC logs, firmware updates), drop them in the shared folder and ping me. We'll turn this into an RCA ticket and include mitigation playbook (drain/automatic fallback + rate-limiting).
Infra-Observer-Bot: Thread closed for initial mitigation. Ongoing: RCA tracking in ticket RCA-1794506789.
Carla (Eng Runtime): Quick question for RCA: do we have historical frequency of AER/ECC on that rack? Might suggest aging hardware. If someone can pull 30d aggregate, add to artifacts.
Maya (ML Infra): I'll schedule a follow-up postmortem meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC. Invitees: oncall rotation, SRE, ML infra, runtime, support.
Benji (Support): Noted — I'll include customer-dk and customer-xl contacts in our postmortem outreach list.
Eli (SRE): Closing notes for now: incident mitigated, suspected noisy neighbor causing PCIe/AER cascades -> node instability -> customer impact small but non-trivial. RCA ticket will track final root cause when provider returns hardware traces.
